description: Draw a chemical structure or reaction as a publication-style figure (ChemDraw-like skeletal formula) with the Lone Pair editor's renderer. Give SMILES, reaction SMILES, InChI, a molfile, a ChemDraw file, or a compound name with name=true. Refused, with the reason, instead of drawn wrongly: SMILES that cannot be read, aromatic rings that cannot alternate single and double bonds, and atoms with too many bonds (unless `as_written`). The result carries `drawing` (Lone Pair JSON to pass to edit_drawing or back in as `input`) and `notes` (anything changed on reading or lost in the format). The SVG and PNG hold the drawing inside them, so they reopen for editing at lonepair.app. Not for a scheme built from separate reactant and product lists (use render_reaction), for changing an earlier figure (use edit_drawing), for numbers only (use analyze), or for molecules placed over a picture (use compose_figure).

as_written.description: Draw atoms that have too many bonds instead of refusing the structure. Default false.

chair.description: With projection chair: stable (default) draws the chair with the larger groups equatorial; flipped draws the other chair (the ring flip).

color.description: black (default); cpk to colour heteroatoms (N blue, O red, S yellow, halogens green); or one colour as #rrggbb for every line and label, such as #ffffff over a dark picture.

dpi.description: PNG resolution, 300 by default; 600 for print.

embed.description: For a structure that goes into a larger figure (an SVG or HTML figure you build, or a picture an image model made): format svg or png only. The SVG gets its own id, data-smiles, data-formula and data-inchikey, and px sizes; the result's `embed` gives its box, the drawn bond length and each atom's position (atom n = the n-th atom of the input), and how to place it. Place it whole and scale it uniformly; never redraw or retouch it. Default false.

embed_id.description: With embed: the id for this structure in your figure (letters, digits, - and _). Give one when the same structure appears twice. Default: lp- and the start of its InChIKey.

format.description: png (default; returned as an image), svg (returned as text), pdf or eps (returned as base64 in `data_base64`).

highlight.description: Highlight parts of the structure with a coloured band under them, e.g. the atoms that react: [{ "atoms": [1, 2, 3], "color": "#ffe066" }]. Atoms are numbered from 1 in input order; bonds between listed atoms are highlighted too, and `bonds` adds others. SVG and PNG only.

bonds.description: Bonds as pairs of atom numbers.

input.description: The structure as text: SMILES, reaction SMILES (reactants>agents>products), InChI, a molfile, RXN, SD file, CDXML, CML or Marvin text, or a Lone Pair drawing (the JSON from an earlier result, or the SVG text of an earlier figure).

name.description: Set to true when `input` is a compound name (e.g. "aspirin") rather than a structure. The name is sent to PubChem to find the structure; this is the only network call the server makes. Short text that is valid SMILES (such as "CO") is read as SMILES, with a note, and not sent. Default false.

opaque.description: White background instead of transparent (SVG, PNG). Default false.

outline_text.description: SVG: draw atom labels and text as outlines instead of text, so the figure looks the same in any program, with or without the fonts. Default false.

projection.description: skeletal (default): flat rings, stereo as wedges. chair: a six-membered ring as a chair, groups axial or equatorial. haworth: a five- or six-membered ring (furanose, pyranose) flat, groups up or down. fischer: an open chain down the page, each stereocentre a cross. Each is drawn from the stereo and only if it reads back as the same structure; one ring, not fused. `notes` says where each group went.

stereoisomers.description: all: draw every stereoisomer of the structure side by side (each stereocentre and E/Z double bond both ways; a meso form once), each labelled R/S and E/Z by atom number. Up to 16; more is refused. Works with projection chair.

style.description: Journal style. acs = ACS Document 1996 (default), rsc = RSC, nature = Nature Reviews, slides = heavier lines for slides.

name: draw
title: Draw a structure
